Xor.label: XOR
Xor.help: Fastest. Easy to undo for someone who looks.

Aes256.label: AES-256
Aes256.help: More work to undo, and slower at run time.

Switch.label: Switch flattening
Switch.help: Splits each method into blocks that a dispatcher runs in a shuffled order.

OpaquePredicate.label: Opaque conditions
OpaquePredicate.help: Adds checks whose outcome is fixed but not obvious to a reader.

Combined.label: Combined
Combined.help: Applies both. The hardest to read, and the biggest cost.

Unreadable.label: Unreadable
Unreadable.help: Look-alike or non-printing characters. Hard to read and to retype.

Sequential.label: Sequential
Sequential.help: Short names in order, such as a, b, c. Small output and easy to follow in a symbol map.

Hash.label: Hash
Hash.help: Names made from a hash of the original plus a random value picked for each run, so the names differ from build to build.

Random.label: Random
Random.help: Random letters and digits that change on every build.

win-x64.label: Native (win-x64)
win-x64.help: A native launcher for Windows x64 replaces the managed file. The .NET runtime must be installed on the target machine.

portable.label: Portable
portable.help: Uses a managed launcher instead of the native one.

symbolRenaming.name: Symbol renaming
symbolRenaming.summary: Replaces type, member and namespace names
symbolRenaming.what: Replaces the names of types, methods, fields, properties, events and namespaces with names that carry no meaning. Your code behaves exactly as before, but a reader of the output sees a.c instead of OrderService.CalculateTotal. Every level starts from this protection.
good: It can break code that looks names up as text: reflection, serialization and XAML bindings.
Keep the symbol map. You need it to read stack traces from the protected build.
Public names are renamed too, unless you preserve the public API.

options.label: Rename these
options.help: Turn off a kind to leave those names as they are.

options.label: Preserve public API
options.help: Leave public names alone. Turn this on for libraries other code compiles against.

options.label: Preserve XAML bindings
options.help: Keeps the names of public properties on types that look bindable (names ending in View or ViewModel, INotifyPropertyChanged, dependency properties), so bindings by property name still resolve. It does not keep type names: leave types that XAML names out of the protection with an exclusion.

stringEncryption.name: String encryption
stringEncryption.what: Encrypts each string literal and replaces it with a call that decrypts it when the program runs. The text no longer appears in the file, so a quick search through the binary finds nothing readable.
good: A small run-time cost, because strings are decrypted as they are used.
Standard and Aggressive turn this on. Minimal leaves strings as they are.

securityNote.title: Obfuscation, not confidentiality.
securityNote.text: The key to decrypt each string ships inside the output assembly, so anyone who runs or inspects it can recover the text: XOR trivially, AES-256 with a little more effort. This raises the cost of casual reverse engineering. Do not ship real secrets such as keys, tokens or credentials in an assembly and rely on it.

options.label: Minimum length
options.help: Shorter strings are left as they are.

constantEncryption.name: Constant encryption
constantEncryption.what: Encrypts integer, long, float and double constants in your code and replaces them with expressions that are worked out when the program runs.
good: Constants in hot loops are worked out every time, so those loops run slower.
Very common values such as 0, 1 and -1 are skipped by default, since hiding them costs more than it protects.

securityNote.title: Obfuscation, not confidentiality.
securityNote.text: The key to decrypt each constant ships inside the output assembly, so anyone who runs or inspects it can recover the values: XOR trivially, AES-256 with a little more effort. This raises the cost of casual reverse engineering. Do not ship real secrets such as keys, tokens or credentials in an assembly and rely on it.

options.label: Hide these kinds
options.help: Turn off a kind to leave those constants as they are.

options.label: Integer threshold
options.help: Integers whose size is below this are left as they are. The default of 2 skips -1, 0 and 1.

options.label: Skip common float values
options.help: Leaves 0.0f, 1.0f and -1.0f as they are.

options.label: Skip common double values
options.help: Leaves 0.0, 1.0 and -1.0 as they are.

resourceEncryption.name: Resource encryption
resourceEncryption.what: Encrypts the resources embedded in the assembly, such as images and text files, and decrypts them when the program reads them.
good: Large resources take longer to load the first time they are used.
Tools that read resources straight from the file, without running your program, will no longer find them.
Only calls to GetManifestResourceStream on an assembly or module are rewritten. Resources read any other way stay encrypted, and the run warns when no call was rewritten.

securityNote.title: Obfuscation, not confidentiality.
securityNote.text: The key to decrypt the resources ships inside the output assembly, so anyone who runs or inspects it can recover the content: XOR trivially, AES-256 with a little more effort. This raises the cost of casual reverse engineering. Do not ship real secrets such as keys, tokens or credentials in an assembly and rely on it.

controlFlow.name: Control flow
controlFlow.summary: Rearranges method bodies so they are hard to read
controlFlow.what: Rewrites the structure of each method so that its steps no longer read top to bottom. The method still does the same work, but a decompiler shows a loop around a large switch instead of the logic you wrote.
good: Slower in hot loops, since every step goes through the dispatcher.
The output file is larger.
Stack traces are harder to read. Keep the symbol map.

options.label: Intensity
options.help: How much of each method is rearranged. Higher is harder to read and slower.

referenceProxy.name: Reference proxy
referenceProxy.summary: Routes calls through generated helper methods
referenceProxy.what: Replaces direct calls with calls to generated helper methods, which hides which method calls which.
good: Adds one extra call to every proxied call.
Calls into your own code are proxied by default. Calls into other libraries are an option.

options.label: Proxy calls to other libraries
options.help: Also hides calls into the .NET libraries and third-party code. Turning this on turns the reference proxy on too.

methodEncryption.name: Method body encryption
methodEncryption.summary: Stores method bodies encrypted in the file
methodEncryption.what: Keeps method bodies encrypted in the file. A start-up routine decrypts them in memory when the assembly loads, before the methods are compiled to run.
good: Each method has its own key. Generic methods are left as they are.
If a body cannot be decrypted, the method stays unreadable. Run your tests against the protected build.
The protected file works on Windows only.

securityNote.title: Obfuscation, not confidentiality.
securityNote.text: The keys to decrypt the method bodies ship inside the output assembly, so anyone who runs or inspects it can recover the code. This raises the cost of casual reverse engineering. Do not ship real secrets such as keys, tokens or credentials in an assembly and rely on it.

virtualization.name: Virtualization
virtualization.summary: Runs selected methods in a small interpreter
virtualization.what: Translates eligible methods into instructions for a small interpreter that ships with the output. The instruction set is shuffled and masked differently on every build.
good: Only some methods can be translated. Methods with exception handling, generics, by-reference parameters, constructors, switch statements or typeof are left as they are.
Translated methods run slower. Use it on a few sensitive methods, not on hot paths.
It is off at every level. Turning it on moves you to Custom.
A deterrent that raises the effort for a reader. It does not keep anything confidential.

antiDebug.name: Debugger check
antiDebug.what: Adds a check that notices a debugger attached to the running program.
good: Your own debugger will trip it too. Test the protected build without one attached.
On NativeAOT, Unity IL2CPP and Blazor WebAssembly it stays available, but leaves out the Windows-specific check.

antiTamper.name: Integrity check
antiTamper.summary: Verifies the file has not been modified
antiTamper.what: Adds a check at start-up that the file has not been changed since it was protected.
good: Changing the protected file afterwards, for example by patching it, makes the check fail.
The check runs at the points you choose below.

options.label: Check at the entry point
options.help: Verifies the file when the program's main method starts.

options.label: Check at module start-up
options.help: Verifies the file as soon as the assembly loads, before any of your code runs. Works for libraries too.

antiDump.name: Memory image guard
antiDump.summary: Makes in-process memory snapshots less useful
antiDump.what: Wipes the file headers from the running program's memory, and patches the Windows function that writes a memory dump so it does nothing inside your own process.
good: It works on x86 and x64. It is skipped on ARM64.
Tools that dump the process from outside are not affected, so this raises the effort only a little.

antiDecompiler.name: Decompiler resistance
antiDecompiler.summary: Adds decoy types that clutter decompiler output
antiDecompiler.what: Adds decoy types and methods that make decompiler output longer and harder to follow.
good: The output file grows with every decoy you add.
Decoys do not stop a determined reader. They add noise.
The decoy attributes make name-based detectors report another tool. They do not block tools that undo obfuscation.

options.label: Add decoy types and methods
options.help: Adds types and methods that do nothing, so real code is harder to find.

options.label: Decoy types
options.help: How many decoy types to add.

options.label: Decoy methods per type
options.help: How many decoy methods to put in each decoy type.

options.label: Mark as not for disassembly
options.help: Adds the attribute that asks IL disassemblers not to open the file. Current tools ignore it.

options.label: Add look-alike tool attributes
options.help: Adds attributes that other obfuscators leave behind, to mislead tools that detect which obfuscator was used.

assemblyMerge.name: Merge assemblies
assemblyMerge.summary: Combines the inputs into one file
assemblyMerge.what: Combines all included assemblies into one file.
good: Needs two or more included assemblies, and every included file must be an assembly: with a C# source file included, Merge does not apply.
With no output folder set, the result is written next to the first input.

options.label: Make merged types internal
options.help: Hides the merged types from other code. Turn this off if other code must still use them.

dependencyEmbedding.name: Embed dependencies
dependencyEmbedding.summary: Packs referenced DLLs inside the output
dependencyEmbedding.what: Packs the DLLs your program references into the output and loads them from there.
good: Only DLLs that sit next to the input and that the input refers to are packed.
The packed DLLs are stored as resources named Obfy.Embedded.* inside the output.

options.label: Include
options.help: File names to pack, one pattern per line. * matches any characters.

options.label: Exclude
options.help: File names to leave out, one pattern per line. These win over the include list.

packing.name: Native packing
packing.summary: Wraps the result in a native launcher
packing.what: Replaces the managed file with a small native launcher that loads your program into the .NET runtime. When several assemblies are protected together, each one with an entry point is packed.
good: Needs an input with an entry point, so it suits applications, not libraries.
The result still needs the .NET runtime on the machine. It is not self-contained and not compiled ahead of time.
It is off at every level. Turning it on moves you to Custom.

securityNote.title: Obfuscation, not confidentiality.
securityNote.text: The key that unpacks your program is stored in the launcher file, so anyone who inspects it can recover the original assembly. Do not ship real secrets such as keys, tokens or credentials and rely on packing.

signing.name: Strong-name signing
signing.summary: Signs the output with your key file
signing.what: Signs the protected output with the key file you choose.
good: Use an .snk, .pfx or .p12 file.
A .pfx or .p12 file needs the name of an environment variable that holds its password. The password itself is never stored in the settings.
Signing runs before packing, so a packed native launcher is not strong-name signed.

options.label: Key file
options.help: The .snk, .pfx or .p12 file to sign with.

options.label: Password variable
options.help: The name of an environment variable that holds the password. Needed for .pfx and .p12 files, not for .snk.

metadataRemoval.name: Metadata removal
metadataRemoval.summary: Strips debug information and compiler attributes
metadataRemoval.what: Removes debug information, and a short list of compiler and debugger attributes.
good: Without debug information a protected build cannot be debugged line by line.

Remove attributes drops nine compiler and debugger attributes only: CompilerGenerated, Nullable, NullableContext, DebuggerNonUserCode, DebuggerStepThrough, DebuggerHidden, DebuggerDisplay, DebuggerBrowsable and SuppressMessage. Your own attributes are kept.
This protection is on while any of its options is on.

options.label: Remove debug information
options.help: Drops the references to the .pdb file.

options.label: Remove attributes
options.help: Drops nine compiler and debugger attributes, such as Nullable and DebuggerStepThrough. Your own attributes are kept.

options.label: Remove documentation
options.help: Drops the XML documentation.

watermark.name: Watermark
watermark.summary: Stamps a customer or build id into the output
watermark.what: Stamps an id of your choice into the output assembly, so you can tell which customer or build a copy came from. The stamp is stored as an attribute that renaming and metadata removal leave alone.
good: Anyone who inspects the assembly can read the id. Do not put anything private in it.
One id per customer means one build per customer.
It does not stop copying. It lets you trace a copy.

options.label: Id
options.help: A customer name or build number. Anyone who inspects the assembly can read it.

incremental.name: Incremental cache
incremental.summary: Skips inputs that have not changed
incremental.what: Remembers the result for each input and skips inputs that have not changed since the last run.
good: An input counts as changed when its bytes, the settings or the Obfy version change.
It is off at every level. Turning it on moves you to Custom.
A cache file that is locked or damaged is treated as no cache.

scope.name: Inclusions and exclusions
scope.what: Rules decide which types and members protection leaves alone, and optionally which ones it is limited to.
good: Type and method patterns match the short name only (OrderService, not MyApp.Models.OrderService); namespace patterns match the namespace. * matches any characters, ? matches one, and case is ignored.
A name that matches an exclusion is always left alone.
Leave the inclusions empty to protect everything that is not excluded.

lists.label: Leave these namespaces alone
lists.help: One pattern per line. Generated code that other tools refer to by name is a good fit.

lists.label: Leave these types alone
lists.help: One pattern per line. Keeps names of the data types your API sends over the wire.

lists.label: Leave these methods alone
lists.help: One pattern per line. Keeps method names that are looked up as text.

lists.label: Only these namespaces
lists.help: One pattern per line. When any inclusion is listed, only matching names are protected.

lists.label: Only these types
lists.help: One pattern per line. A type matches when its namespace or its name matches.

lists.label: Only these methods
lists.help: One pattern per line. A method matches when its name matches.
